Can A $0,1 Mini PC Run Minecraft?

I recently found a $0,1 Mini PC, and at that price, I expected it to be completely useless. The hardware is extremely old, the condition is far from perfect, and there was no guarantee that it would even turn on. However, I wanted to give this $0,1 Mini PC one final chance by testing it with Minecraft.

Before launching the game, I inspected the $0,1 Mini PC, cleaned the internal components, and checked whether its processor, memory, and storage were still working. This tiny computer was never designed for modern gaming, but Minecraft is known for running on almost anything.

To give the $0,1 Mini PC the best possible chance, I installed a lightweight operating system, tested several older Minecraft versions, and reduced every graphics setting I could find. I also tried performance modifications to see whether the $0,1 Mini PC could reach a playable frame rate.

Throughout the video, I monitor FPS, loading times, CPU usage, RAM consumption, temperatures, and overall stability. Can the $0,1 Mini PC successfully load a Minecraft world? Can the $0,1 Mini PC handle basic exploration without freezing? And can the $0,1 Mini PC provide an enjoyable gaming experience despite costing almost nothing?

The final results were much more interesting than I expected. This experiment proves that even extremely cheap and outdated computers can still have some hidden potential.
